findings.claim: The strict exception/no-new-side-effects requirement remains unmet. Round 2 establishes an observable allocation-size difference at every enabled call rather than eliminating the round-1 concern. Equal allocation counts and equal results when forcibly failing the nth allocation do not establish equivalent allocation-failure behaviour when the requested sizes differ. The authorization has not been amended to permit this upstream implementation difference.
findings.evidence: The reference reports, for example, "stmt 0 where='tile:left' allocs=2 seq=P sizes=40,40," while the candidate reports "stmt 0 where='tile:left' allocs=2 seq=P sizes=31,40,". The runner accepts this through comparisons using "sed 's/ sizes=.*//'" and reports "MEASURED DIFFERENCE (host template internals): allocation sizes differ:".

findings.where: Runtime equivalence probe: equiv_main.cpp allocation-failure runs
findings.claim: The fault-injection results are narrower than exception and side-effect equivalence. They test an unconditional failure at each sampled allocation ordinal, not size-dependent failures or actual memory-pressure behaviour. They also do not compare argument-evaluation traces during failing executions: those traces are reset and collected but never included in the failure report. No throwing argument accessor is supplied. These are coverage limitations, not additional demonstrated call-site defects.
findings.evidence: Failure is injected only by "if (g_failAt && g_allocs == g_failAt) throw std::bad_alloc();". Each failure run sets "g_seqLen = 0", but its report is only "fail@%ld -> %s, emitted=%s". The supplied accessors record tokens and return values; none explicitly injects an argument-evaluation exception.

findings.where: Probe E runner: NEG2 diagnostic acceptance
findings.claim: The all-file filtering improves round 1, but NEG2 still permits unrelated constant-expression errors. Its allowance is not restricted to the stated consequential <string> diagnostic: any matched error line containing 'is not a constant expression' passes. Thus an expected diagnostic plus an unrelated error of that form can still be accepted. This is a residual acceptance-condition weakness, not evidence that the reported runs contained such an error.
findings.evidence: For NEG2 the runner sets "ALLOW=\"$RX|is not a constant expression\"" and computes NBAD by filtering every matched error line against that unrestricted expression.

notes:
1. All five calls preserve DEBUG and, on successful formatting, the diagnostic bytes. The unchanged payload format strings and argument expressions support this independently of the sampled output. Both templates check m_logsEnabled and then the TRACE condition before formatting. Argument expressions still evaluate before function entry, including with logging disabled. The added location and format literals introduce no side-effecting argument expression. The probes show matching recorded accessor order within each compiler; GCC and Clang differ from each other in both versions. Neither source version specifies a common left-to-right order among arguments, and the mocks do not establish all effects of the real plugin argument types. Both versions propagate uncaught exceptions from arguments or formatting; exact exception behaviour is not established because allocation requests differ. As an illustrative hypothetical, not an observed result, a replacement allocator that rejects a 31-byte request but accepts a 40-byte request would distinguish the first sampled call even though the nth-allocation injection results match. Allocation sizes are already demonstrably observable in this harness.

2. All five old calls select the 0.56.2 formatting template, and all five new calls select the 0.57 formatting template. Each new call has at least four total arguments, excluding both non-template overloads by arity. Both templates ultimately call the two-argument sink. The three-argument (level, loc, str) trap is real, but none of these five new calls risks it. TrapBinds establishes that its expression is well-formed; identifying the selected overload also requires inspecting the supplied overload set.

3. The supplied diff changes only the five authorized logging statements. It contains no render-pass, GL, timer, hook, lifecycle or ownership edits.

4. The runtime comparison is non-vacuous. It extracts the five actual statements, requires five matches, fails with the unmodified baseline used as candidate, and detects compiling runtime mutations after the edit. The supplied -H trace identifies the oldinc Logger.hpp; the old calls failing against the installed header independently corroborate that the working reference was not using that installed header. The compile commands support the same intended old-header selection for both compilers. The sinks and constructor are probe replacements, so this is a real-template comparison, not full host/plugin runtime validation. Runtime negatives now ignore the known size difference and compare all three configured states, making their detections meaningful for the introduced mutations. The five reference statements are DEBUG, so toggling m_isTrace does not itself exercise reference TRACE suppression; the candidate TRACE mutation and identical gate source provide narrower supporting evidence. NewShape checks expression well-formedness for synthetic types, not template-body behaviour or complete real-type semantics. The logger assertion checks its declared type, not ownership behaviour generally. Inverting assertions verifies that those assertions are enforced, not independent semantic correctness.

5. The diagnostic comparison is internally consistent as reported. GCC reproduces the P5 baseline at 73 and removes six Log-related errors, leaving 67 persistent and zero new. Clang with P5 flags reproduces 96 and removes five, leaving 91 persistent and zero new. The Makefile-flags Clang comparison is separately 92 to 87; the four narrowing diagnostics explicitly reconcile it with the P5-flags run. These results support removal of the targeted diagnostics, not equivalence or a complete successful build. The remaining build failure and absence of a .so are disclosed. Geometry and tooltip passes do not resolve the logging allocation difference.

The main rejection is unchanged in substance: the newly measured allocation difference needs an explicit authorization exception or a different implementation. Showing that the preformat alternative introduces disabled-logging allocations does not make the selected implementation strictly equivalent.
